title: Adani Wilmar Limited (AWL)
abstract: The total size of the edible oils market in India was estimated to be 13 million tons (mt) out of which imports amounted to about 4 mt. This made India the largest importer of edible oils in the world. Various edible oils are consumed in the India depending on the regional tastes and preferences. A differential in the duties on oil seed and oils made it favorable to import edible oils instead of oilseeds. Similarly, a differential duty between the refined oil and the raw oil encouraged the import of raw oil in order to support the domestic refineries. Adani Wilmar Limited (AWL) was a part of the Adani group, which started as a trading company mainly into exports of commodities. The group had recently entered into the infrastructure sector with the building of the Mundra port. The group had formed a joint venture with Wilmar Trading of Singapore to enter into the edible oil business. The company was setting up a re.nery with capacity of 600 tons per day. It planned to sell half of the production as bulk oil and the rest as packed oil. The company viewed supply chain management as one of the important means to get a competitive edge. Approximately 70% of the total logistics cost was accounted for by transportation cost. Some of the key decisions the company faced was the location of the warehouses, mode choice and routing.

summary.oneLiner: Adani Wilmar Limited leveraged supply chain management and strategic infrastructure, such as the Mundra port, to enter the competitive Indian edible oil market.
summary.overview: Adani Wilmar Limited (AWL), a joint venture between the Adani Group and Wilmar Trading, entered the Indian edible oil market by setting up refinery operations. Because India is the world's largest importer of edible oils, the company aimed to gain a competitive advantage through efficient supply chain management. Key operational challenges for the firm included optimizing transportation costs, which made up 70% of their total logistics spend, and making strategic choices regarding warehouse locations and routing. The firm balanced its business model by selling a mix of bulk and packaged oil to meet regional consumer preferences.
summary.question: How did Adani Wilmar Limited approach its market entry and supply chain strategy within the context of India's import-dependent edible oil industry?

findings: The company viewed supply chain management as a critical mechanism for achieving a competitive edge in the market.
Logistics costs were significantly impacted by transportation, which accounted for approximately 70% of the total logistics expense.
Strategic infrastructure, such as the Mundra port, supported the group's expansion into the edible oil sector.
summary.whyItMatters: The case illustrates how operational decisions, specifically in logistics and supply chain network design, are pivotal for new entrants in commodity-based industries with high import dependency.
